newsitem.title: CHILE: Russian ship pulled off rocks in Antarctica.
newsitem.headline: Russian ship pulled off rocks in Antarctica.

text.p: A Russian scientific ship that ran aground on rocks in Antarctica was towed free by a Chilean naval ship on Sunday, navy spokesmen said on Monday.

The naval vessel pulled the Professor Khromov off rocks in the Neumayer Channel off the Antarctic Peninsula, spokesmen in the southern city of Punta Arenas said. The rocks did not pierce the ship's reinforced hull and there was no oil leak, they said.

All 36 passengers, most of them scientists of various nationalities, and some of the crew were evacuated onto another Russian ship, the Alla Tarasova, and will continue their cruise along the Antarctic coast, they said.

The 220-foot (72-metre), 2,100-tonne Khromov was heading on its own steam for Punta Arenas, near the southern tip of South America, to repair its damaged hull, one spokesman said. "It has some dents in the hull but we can't know how serious they are until it reaches Punta Arenas," he said.

The ship struck rocks just before midnight on Saturday as it sailed through the narrow channel between Anvers and Wiencke Islands, an area of rich wildlife including penguins, seals and whales. Passengers included Russian, Canadian, German and U.S. scientists, radio reports from Punta Arenas said.
